en.headline: Local artist LeonLollipop’s Gloomie Museum exhibition runs at Harbour City until 25…
en.dek: The first solo show of the cheek-resting cat character features the 100th portrait, reimagined classical works with Hong Kong scenery, and terracotta-style cat sculptures.
body: Hong Kong artist Leon Lai, known as LeonLollipop, is holding his first solo exhibition, “Gloomie Museum”, at Gallery by the Harbour in Harbour City until 25 October.

The show centres on his signature Gloomie cat, which has appeared in large-scale murals around the city. It includes the debut of the 100th Gloomie portrait, titled Gloomie Lisa, a reworking of Leonardo da Vinci’s Mona Lisa set against a Kai Tak backdrop, along with other pieces that place classical art styles against familiar Hong Kong locations such as Stanley and Sheung Wan.

Seventeen sculptures are also on display, seven of them interpreting Western art masters in feline form and ten forming a “Kitty Army” inspired by the Terracotta Warriors. The gallery is open from 11am to 9pm daily. Visitors can collect stamps at four stations to complete a postcard illustration.

zh.headline: 本地藝術家LeonLollipop「Gloomie Museum托腭貓藝術館」海港城展至10月25日
zh.dek: 首個個人展覽展出系列第100幅作品《Gloomie Lisa》，以香港地景重新演繹經典名畫，並設有兵馬俑造型貓士兵雕塑。
body: 本地藝術家Leon Lai（LeonLollipop）正於海港城美術館舉行首個個人展覽「Gloomie Museum托腭貓藝術館」，展期至10月25日。
展覽以藝術家標誌性的托腭貓角色Gloomie為主角。Gloomie過往曾以大型壁畫出現於本港不同角落。今次展出系列第100幅作品《Gloomie Lisa》，將達文西《蒙娜麗莎》以Gloomie形象及啟德景觀重新呈現，其他作品亦把經典藝術風格置於赤柱、上環等熟悉本地場景中。
現場另有17件雕塑，其中7件以貓的形象演繹西方藝術大師風格，10件則組成靈感來自兵馬俑的「貓咪軍隊」。美術館每日上午11時至晚上9時開放。訪客可在四個蓋章站收集印章，完成一張明信片插圖。
